title: Reliability and Production Readiness
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of reliability and production readiness using at least one correct term from the lesson.
Interpret or adapt a small Kotlin example that demonstrates reliability and production readiness.
Identify one relevant edge case, debugging step, or version/platform constraint.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Reliability and Production Readiness** as part of **Software Engineering, Security, and Performance**. Treat external input, dependencies, credentials, error handling, observability, and recovery as production design concerns rather than afterthoughts. Use the subtopics—Logging and Observability, Configuration Management, Graceful Failure and Recovery—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Professional applications need repeatable tests, clear APIs, dependable dependencies, security checks, and observable failures. Apply this concept in small steps before integrating it into a larger project.

content_blocks.title: How to reason about it
content_blocks.text: Start with logging and observability. Then compare it with configuration management. Identify the input, state, dependency, or branch that determines the result. The snippet is a static reference for CodeLeaf and is not executed in the lesson page.

items.text: Logging and Observability is one part of reliability and production readiness. Connect its definition to the example, identify the input/state it changes, and verify the expected behavior with a small test case.

items.title: Graceful Failure and Recovery
items.text: Graceful Failure and Recovery helps make behavior observable and repeatable. Define the expected result, include a boundary or failure case, and preserve enough diagnostic information to locate the cause without leaking sensitive data.

content_blocks.run_instructions: Run in the project that declares the necessary JVM, coroutine, networking, database, or serialization dependencies. Never commit real secrets.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the documented starting values, rerun the smallest test, and compare the result with the expected output. If behavior differs, check the compiler/plugin/runtime versions and the active target before changing more than one thing.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake to avoid
content_blocks.text: Reliability and Production Readiness removes the need to test boundary conditions or verify the chosen runtime/library version.

content_blocks.title: Troubleshooting and reset
content_blocks.text: If the example fails, first confirm which runtime/project type the snippet requires. Read the first useful compiler or runtime message, check imports and declared dependencies, reduce the example to a minimal case, and rerun. For target-specific code, use the target toolchain rather than assuming a console or browser runner can execute it.

content.task: Try it yourself: create a small variation that demonstrates reliability and production readiness. Write down your predicted result first, run it in the correct local project, then explain one boundary case involving logging and observability.
